xychart.comment: Begin at the lowercase detector prefix and accept either bounded beta spelling. xychart.md#detection: The lexer then reads the header, the keyword `xychart-beta` or the keyword `xychart`, compared case-insensitively and not followed by a word character (see [The statement context](#the-statement-context)).

patterns.comment: Read another bounded header before statements. xychart.md#diagram-and-statements: A header may follow another, on its line or on a later one, and may carry an orientation, but no header follows a statement.

Read the orientation as a listed fixed value; enclosing text contexts keep quoted words as text. xychart.md#detection: The **orientation** is the keyword `vertical` or `horizontal`, compared case-insensitively, right after a header, with whitespace other than a line feed between them, or with whitespace and line feeds after whitespace between them (see [Line breaks](#units-and-contexts)); a statement may follow it on its line.
patterns.name: constant.language.mermaid

patterns.comment: Read an accessibility keyword and its delimiter in the local context, retaining its distinct whitespace and end-of-text rules. xychart.md#accessibility-values: `accTitle` and `:` enter the accessibility title context, and `accDescr` and `:` the accessibility description context. Each reads the whitespace after the `:`, line feeds included, and then the rest of the line as an `acc-title-text` or an `acc-description-text` unit, and leaves. xychart.md#accessibility-values: Without a `}`, the text runs to the end of the text. common.md#comment-lines: Comment lines are recognized independently of the diagram's syntax and of the context the lexer is in.

Read the colon and line value without consuming a possible comment boundary in the opening gap. xychart.md#accessibility-values: `accTitle` and `:` enter the accessibility title context, and `accDescr` and `:` the accessibility description context. Each reads the whitespace after the `:`, line feeds included, and then the rest of the line as an `acc-title-text` or an `acc-description-text` unit, and leaves. common.md#comment-lines: Comment lines are recognized independently of the diagram's syntax and of the context the lexer is in.

Read description text through its first closing brace, leaving separator-led common comments outside the value. xychart.md#accessibility-values: `accDescr`, whitespace, and `{` enter the description block context, which reads the whitespace after the `{` and then every character up to the next `}` as a `description-block-text` unit, empty when the `}` follows the whitespace, reads the `}` as a `}` unit, and leaves. common.md#comment-lines: Comment lines are recognized independently of the diagram's syntax and of the context the lexer is in.

Read a chart title until the next statement, separator or physical line end. xychart.md#titles: The title is words or one string, not both, and never empty: `title` alone, `title` and a space at the end of the text, and `title ""` are rejected. common.md#comment-lines: Comment lines are recognized independently of the diagram's syntax and of the context the lexer is in.

Read an axis title and data in the axis context, keeping category digits as text. xychart.md#the-axis-context: `x-axis` and `y-axis` enter the axis context. xychart.md#the-axis-context: It ends at the end of its statement: a line break leaves it and is a `newline` unit, and a `;` and a keyword leave it and are read in the context below, but for `accDescr` with `{`, which enters the description block context on top of it, so that the axis context goes on after the `}`. common.md#comment-lines: Comment lines are recognized independently of the diagram's syntax and of the context the lexer is in.

Read a category list with textual digits. xychart.md#the-category-context: `[` in the axis context enters the category context, and `]` leaves it. xychart.md#the-category-context: So digits are words there: `[Q1]`, `[1, 2]`, `[-1, +2, .5]`, and `[1.5, -2]` are categories, and the words of a category, with whitespace between them or not, are one category.

Read the three-character range arrow. xychart.md#the-axis-context: A range needs the three characters of the arrow together: `1-->-2` is a range, and `1 - -> 2`, `1 -- > 2`, and `1 -> 2` are rejected.
patterns.name: keyword.operator.arrow.mermaid

patterns.comment: Read a plot title and its values, keeping title digits as text. xychart.md#the-plot-context: `line` and `bar` enter the plot context. xychart.md#the-plot-context: So digits are words in the title of a plot: `line Q1 [1]`, `bar 2024 [1]`, `line a-1 [1]`, `line -5 [2]`, and `line 1.5 [2]` have the titles `Q1`, `2024`, `a-1`, `-5`, and `1.5`. common.md#comment-lines: Comment lines are recognized independently of the diagram's syntax and of the context the lexer is in.

Read a plot's bracketed values and optional quoted labels. xychart.md#plots: A plot statement is `line` or `bar`, a title or none, and one or more values in brackets, separated by commas. xychart.md#plots: A value may be followed by a label, a string, with or without whitespace between them, on a line and on a bar.
Read a semicolon as a statement separator. xychart.md#diagram-and-statements: A `;` ends a line as a line feed does, and empty lines and empty statements change nothing.
patterns.name: punctuation.separator.semicolon.mermaid

xychart-string.comment: Reuse plain double-quoted strings without escapes. xychart.md#strings: A string has no escape: a second `"` ends it, so `"a""b"` is two strings.

xychart-word.comment: Read word units as labels, preserving directives inside a run of letters or digits. xychart.md#the-statement-context: So a text without quotes is made of letters of ASCII, digits, and `-`, `_`, `.`, `+`, `=`, `*`, `&`, and `#`, a `#` being no comment: `title T # c` has the title `T#c`. xychart.md#directives-inside-units: The **text units** are a `word`, an `acc-title-text`, an `acc-description-text`, and a `description-block-text`. common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary: A directive is trivia and not diagram text.
xychart-word.name: string.unquoted.mermaid

xychart-number.comment: Read a number in axis ranges and plot values. xychart.md#the-axis-context: A number has no exponent and no `.` without digits after it: `1e3 --> 5` and `1. --> 2` are rejected, while `.5`, `007`, `-0`, `+1`, and a number of twenty digits are numbers.
xychart-number.name: constant.numeric.mermaid

xychart-comment.comment: Reuse native percent comments outside value text. xychart.md#comments: A comment starts at `%%` where a unit starts and runs to the end of its line, the line feed left out; it belongs to no unit.

xychart-list-separator.comment: Read the separator of categories and plot values. xychart.md#plots: A plot statement is `line` or `bar`, a title or none, and one or more values in brackets, separated by commas.
xychart-list-separator.name: punctuation.separator.comma.mermaid
